messages:
Meera: FYI customer "AcmeHealth" says their SIEM didn't receive any audit events for a ~2h window yesterday (2024-04-01 02:10-04:15 UTC). They sent a few example request_ids: rq_8a3f2c, rq_8a3f9b. Can we triage?
Alex: taking it. are these from the S3 export or the syslog/forwarder?
Meera: they have SIEM forwarding to our S3 export (bucket redwood-exports/acmehealth/audit/) and a direct syslog TLS forwarder as a backup. They see a gap in SIEM UI and the customer can't find events in their Splunk.
Tony: quick checks: our export pipeline shows no 5xxs in that timeframe. infra-pipeline: any ingestion backfills or drops?
infra-pipeline: logging: we saw a transient Kafka consumer rebalance around 2024-04-01T02:09:48Z, some partitions moved, consumer lag spiked ~40s for ~90s, then recovered. No errors >5xx.
Jules (support): customer reports missing events that include admin.role.change events (sensitive). they need proof for audit. escalation to security/compliance required.
Alex: possible causes: 1) export filter applying incorrectly to admin.* events for that tenant, 2) KMS decrypt failure preventing export writing to S3 for that tenant key, 3) SIEM ingestion side (Splunk) dropped items. Which one lines up with rebalances?
Meera: customer uses customer-managed KMS key (cmk:projects/acme/locations/global/keyRings/ah/cryptoKeys/acme-audit). Could a CMK permissions or HSM rotation cause a write failure?
Tony: if PutObject failed due to KMS, we'd have S3 object put errors and retry in exporter. I scanned exporter logs for that bucket: no KMSException logged between 02:05-04:20. However, exporter did emit a schema-compatibility warning at 02:11 for a small batch (schema_v2 vs expected_v3). That caused that batch to be skipped by the exporter v2->v3 safeguard.
Meera: schema-compatibility warning? that could explain admin.* events missing if they were in that batch. what's in the schema change?
Alex: it was a field rename: "actor_id" -> "actor.user_id" (nested). Our CSV-ish legacy consumers expect flat actor_id. exporter v2 has a strict check and will drop batches that don't match target schema to avoid corrupting exports. That matches the exact window.
Jules (support): customer says the missing events' request_ids are definitely in our internal audit store (we verified), just never landed in the S3 export. They need the exported copies.
Tony: plan: 1) confirm internal store has the full raw events for those request_ids, 2) re-run exporter for that time range with a tolerant schema flag (dry-run first), 3) push to a quarantined bucket for re-ingest by Splunk. I'll own 1-2.
Alex: to confirm internal store quickly run: ```SELECT * FROM audit_raw WHERE request_id IN ('rq_8a3f2c','rq_8a3f9b') ORDER BY timestamp;``` I can run that if you don't have access.
Meera: ran the query, both events present in audit_raw with full payloads and correct event_type=admin.role.change. timestamp 2024-04-01T02:12:03Z and 02:13:07Z.
Tony: starting exporter replay now. Using the tolerant mode: `exporter --tenant acmehealth --start 2024-04-01T02:05:00Z --end 2024-04-01T04:20:00Z --schema-tolerance=relaxed --destination=s3://redwood-exports/acmehealth/quarantine/`
infra-pipeline: replay job created job_id=rep_20240401_02_acme_17. No immediate errors. Monitoring upload metrics.
Alex: note for postmortem: we should avoid strict schema-skip for tenant exports without alerting the tenant. Add a flag to surface skipped-batch counts to tenant console.
Jules (support): I'll open a formal incident-ticket and notify the customer: TKT-2024-1874. Include repro steps and ETA.
security-bot: automated notice: audit logs are encrypted at rest with KMS. For customer-managed keys, any exported objects are encrypted with customer's CMK (key name: projects/acme/locations/global/keyRings/ah/cryptoKeys/acme-audit). Verify IAM on that key if you see KMS failures.
Tony: replay completed for job rep_20240401_02_acme_17. 172 events uploaded to quarantine bucket. 2 objects matching request_ids uploaded. No KMS or S3 PutObject errors.
Meera: I pulled the objects and forwarded to customer's Splunk contact. they confirm both events ingested and visible. They need a signed statement for compliance: can infra provide an export manifest with checksums and timestamps?
Alex: yes — manifest generated: ```{
  "job_id": "rep_20240401_02_acme_17",
  "objects": ["s3://redwood-exports/acmehealth/quarantine/part-0001.json.gz"],
  "count": "172",
  "sha256": "d34db33f..."
}``` I'll attach to the ticket.
Jules (support): customer accepted. Closing loop. Action items: 1) add exporter skipped-batch alerting (owner: Alex, due 2024-04-10), 2) add retention note in console for schema compatibility (owner: Meera), 3) run a one-week replay sanity job for all CMK tenants (owner: Tony).
Meera: can we also add a short KB for customers: how to verify their SIEM ingestion and what to check (KMS IAM, S3 prefixes, schema contract)? I'll draft and post in docs.
Tony: small root-cause note: exporter schema-strictness was intentional to avoid corrupting long-term archives. but we need better tenant-visible telemetry before skipping.
Alex: resolution: events restored to customer SIEM, manifest uploaded to TKT-2024-1874, customer satisfied. marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
Jules (support): thanks all — good follow-up. I'll update the ticket and asset the postmortem.
Meera: thanks — closing thread.
